name: Prime DataStreamConsumer stores stale signed oracle reports
summary: Prime's DataStreamConsumer.verifyReport stores any validly signed Chainlink Data Streams report for its feed without checking that it is newer than the stored one, and the adapter chain reading it does no staleness check. Replaying an old PRFI report inflated PRFI's oracle price far above its thin market, so cheap PRFI collateral borrowed the whole WHYPE reserve.
notes: Reset: the consumer was deployed first, but the exploit also needed PRFI listed as collateral and the AaveOracle source for PRFI pointed at the Data Streams stack; that source assignment (an oracle setting rated HIGH) is the latest such change. Later pool writes only touched reserve factor, liquidation bonus, rate strategy and an unrelated listing.
Gross loss is the WHYPE reserve drained from aWHYPE 0xcf4642ef; the attacker's own WHYPE spent on PRFI and the repaid flash loan are not victim assets.
